title: Compute brief - 22 October 2026
description: Meta spent $34.9 billion on capex in Q3, raised the floor of its 2026 range to $135 to 145 billion and went free cash flow negative; it also created a non-voting share class it says can fund infrastructure. Sellers say compute pricing is still rising, Humain lines up 84 MW with NVIDIA, and UK industry warns it has 12 months to win local consent. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Meta goes cash-flow negative and builds a share class to keep spending
lede: The first hyperscaler print of the season says the spending is not slowing, and the cash to pay for it is getting tighter. Meta reported Q3 capex of $34.91 billion including finance lease principal, raised the bottom of its 2026 range to $135 to 145 billion (was $130 to 145 billion) and posted free cash flow of minus $2.12 billion, against plus $10.63 billion a year earlier. It gave no 2027 number but said it expects to keep investing aggressively, and CFO Susan Li said compute remains constrained and Meta has underestimated its needs before. The same release creates a non-voting Class C stock, effective January 2027, which Meta says gives it room to raise capital for infrastructure. Shares fell in early trading on 22 October in a wider AI selloff that took the KOSPI down 3.5%. Sellers of compute say price is holding: SpaceX said its AI unit earned $7.56 billion of revenue in Q3 with new deployments paying back in under a year, Nebius said its Tuesday capacity auction cleared higher and opened public live spot prices, and Humain and NVIDIA laid out up to 84 MW in Saudi Arabia including 50 MW of Vera Rubin for a US client. On the public tape all 70 prints confirmed, including Crusoe's H100 at $3.90 a day after its CEO said H100 prices are above 2023 levels.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.note: Humain and NVIDIA plan up to 84 MW, about 27,000 GPUs: 14 MW of HGX B300 from Q4 2026, then 70 MW of Vera Rubin from June 2027 including 50 MW for an unnamed US client; Vera Rubin phases subject to final agreements (Wire, 22 Oct).

countries.name: United States
countries.note: Google and Voltus expand to a 1 GW Google-funded virtual power plant across PJM, ten times the earlier 100 MW deal (Wire, 22 Oct). Meta 2026 capex range raised at the floor to $135 to 145 billion (Signal).

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.note: SAIL taskforce (NVIDIA, Microsoft, Cisco) tells ministers they have about 12 months to agree a local-benefit compact before US-style opposition threatens construction (Wire, 22 Oct; Guardian exclusive).

countries.name: South Korea
countries.note: Chip exports a record US$27.5 billion for 1 to 20 October, up 222.5% and 44.7% of all exports (Wire, 21 Oct, preliminary customs data). KOSPI fell 3.5% on 22 Oct on AI spending worries.
